predecessors.name: Republic of Peru
predecessors.text: Peru, divided into the North Peruvian and South Peruvian states

predecessors.name: Bolivia
predecessors.text: the Bolivian Republic, whose Tapacarí Congress of 21 June 1836 authorised Santa Cruz to complete the confederation

successors.name: Republic of Peru
successors.text: Peru, 'merged back into a single Peru' after Yungay and Gamarra's declaration of 25 August 1839

successors.name: Bolivia
successors.text: Bolivia ('New Bolivian State'), with Tarija, which 'ultimately remained in Bolivia'

ledger.x: 1836: Santa Cruz founds the Peru-Bolivian Confederation.
1836: Bolivia joins the Confederation the same day.
1837: Chile lands at Islay and occupies Arequipa.

1837: the Treaty of Paucarpata, 17 November 1837, in which Chile agreed to 'withdraw its troops from Confederate territory'; the page gives no date for the departure itself, and Chile repudiated the treaty.
1838: the Confederation holds Argentine border land.
1838: the Chileans leave Lima on 3 November 1838 ('abandoned it on November 3').
1839: the occupied Argentine land is returned.
1839: Yungay breaks the Confederation in Peru.

wars.name: War of the Confederation
wars.outcome: Chilean-Peruvian Restoration victory: the Confederate army was crushed at Yungay on 20 January 1839, Gamarra declared the Confederation dissolved on 25 August 1839 and the Chileans left on 19 October 1839; Peru was merged back into one state and Bolivia kept…

certainty.note: Neither page describes the Confederation's boundaries; the frontier in the Amazon, the Chaco and the Pacific coast of Bolivia (all in Cliopatria's shape) is approximate, and the Argentine border at Tarija was fought over.
